text:
Anya: Quick share — ran a short bench comparing Mistral-7B-v0.9 (open weights) vs Llama-2-7B across A100 (us-west1) and H100 (eu-west1). Focus: prefill vs decode p50/p99, tokens/sec, and $/1M tokens. Links and raw numbers below. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Sam: Nice! can you paste the exact run config?

Anya: Sure — ran single-GPU runs, isolated queues, no multi-GPU. Config:```model: mistral-7b-v0.9
quant: fp16 / int8x4
batching: dynamic, max_batch=8
seq_prefill: 512
seq_decode: 256
kernels: auto (flash/flash2 if available)
region: us-west1 / eu-west1
metrics: prefill_ms, decode_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1M
```

perf-bot: Benchmark job finished (id: perf-1715558888). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/mistral-vs-llama/1715558888/

Kevin: Topline (p50 / tokens/sec / $/1M) — rounding to useful digits:
- A100 (us-west1): Mistral-7B fp16: prefill p50 118ms, decode p50 19ms, tokens/sec 860, ~$3.05/1M.
- H100 (eu-west1): Mistral-7B fp16: prefill p50 86ms, decode p50 16ms, tokens/sec 1120, ~$2.40/1M.
- A100 (us-west1): Llama-2-7B fp16: prefill p50 140ms, decode p50 21ms, tokens/sec 760, ~$3.40/1M.
- H100 (eu-west1): Llama-2-7B fp16: prefill p50 100ms, decode p50 18ms, tokens/sec 980, ~$2.95/1M.

Rachel: Observations: H100 wins across the board for prefill and throughput (esp for longer prefix). Cost delta driven by tokens/sec + instance hourly pricing in region. Numbers above include instance amortized infra overhead ~8%.

Sam: What about quantization? int8x4 on A100/H100? Any quality/regression checks?

Anya: Quick notes on quant: int8x4 lowered cost significantly but had small quality regressions on instr-follow eval set (approx -4% EM for Mistral int8x4, -6% for Llama int8x4). Numbers: 
- A100 Mistral int8x4: tokens/sec 1280, prefill p50 95ms, decode p50 13ms, ~$0.95/1M.
- H100 Mistral int8x4: tokens/sec 1450, prefill p50 70ms, decode p50 12ms, ~$0.80/1M.
Quality drop flagged on our eval harness (eval-id: eval-mistral-171555).

Kevin: Kernel chatter — saw fallbacks on A100 when sequence >1024:
```
WARN kernel_selector: flash_attention_v2 not available for int8x4 on this CUDA ABI -> using gemm_fallback
```
Fallback added 15–25% tail latency in some runs. H100 used flash2 for >1024 and kept latency tight.

Rachel: Capacity sizing quick calc: if product expects 500 QPS with avg 12 tokens generated per request, that's 6000 tokens/sec. Using Mistral on H100 we measured ~1450 tokens/sec per GPU (int8x4). So need ceil(6000/1450)=5 GPUs + safety (can provision 6). On A100 at 1280 tok/s need 5 GPUs as well but p99s were worse; recommend 7 A100 to hit similar tail SLOs.

Sam: Good to know. Any regional diffs beyond instance price? E.g., kernel availability, CUDA driver versions?

Anya: Yes — eu-west1 fleet had newer drivers (CUDA 12.x) and libaries; that unlocked flash2 kernels for our build. us-west1 A100 hosts are on CUDA 11.8 which caused the int8 kernel selector to fallback. Driver/kernel parity is the main culprit.

Kevin: Next steps proposed:
- Re-run int8x4 on A100 after rolling CUDA 12.x in a small pool (sanity).
- Run full eval harness (1000 eval prompts) for Mistral int8x4 vs fp16 to quantify quality delta.
- Long-seq (>2048) runs to stress prefill kernels.

Rachel: Artifacts/grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/infra/mistral-vs-llama?orgId=1&panelId=7 (raw CSV + plot) and CSV: s3://redwood-perf/mistral-vs-llama/1715558888/results.csv

Anya: TL;DR: H100 gives better prefill and throughput, int8x4 gives big $ wins but watch quality and kernel fallbacks on older A100 hosts. Recommendation: Mistral-7B + int8x4 on H100 for cost-sensitive production; run more evals before enabling auto-rollout. :eyes:

perf-bot: Uploaded perf artifacts and eval summary to the thread. (artifacts link above)

Kevin: I'll queue the CUDA-12 A100 small pool test and ping infra.

Sam: Thanks, really helpful — will add a short task to our bring-up checklist to include driver parity + eval-id in PRs. :+1:
